picks.excerpt: Drew Geraci stress-tests Seedance 2.5 with long-form, shot-designed prompts in a new MZed module on ethical AI video, showing how directing language (lens, blocking, continuity) changes generated output.
picks.rationale: Turns prompting into directing craft — concrete language for lens, blocking and continuity that a filmmaker can apply to the next shot list.

picks.excerpt: LA studio Impossible Objects is running AI models locally on HP ZGX Nano desktops, folding artist-driven generative workflows in alongside traditional VFX tools without shipping client plates to the cloud.
picks.rationale: A working studio's answer to NDA-bound generative work: local inference on a desk-side box, no client plates leaving the building.

picks.excerpt: SP Studios rebuilt its LED volume workflow around Brompton Hydra, changing how in-camera VFX shots are lit, calibrated and captured on set.
picks.rationale: Concrete on-set pipeline change for ICVFX — how the volume is calibrated and lit rewrites what has to be fixed in post.

picks.excerpt: Curious Refuge walks through Apple's new photoreal personal-avatar cloning and what near-perfect digital doubles mean for performance capture and on-camera talent in AI filmmaking.
picks.rationale: Consumer-grade photoreal digital doubles land straight on the performance-capture and likeness-consent questions productions are deciding right now.

picks.excerpt: Production designer Brandon Tonner-Connolly breaks down a hand-painted glass matte shot on 'Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma' — an in-camera answer to effects work that would default to digital or generative today.
picks.rationale: A repeatable in-camera technique breakdown — the cheapest way to get an effect that would otherwise be a generative or CG line item.
